key_insight: The paper shows that openly released, high-quality medical and general multimodal training data can produce robust healthcare vision-language models that perform well without losing general capabilities.
clinical_relevance: These models could improve medical image-and-text understanding for clinical and biomedical applications, but they still need careful validation before any real-world use.
method: Built Aloe-Vision-Data, a large filtered mixture of medical and general multimodal plus text-only data.
Trained open Aloe-Vision LVLMs at two scales: 7B and 72B, with full weights and training recipes released.
Created CareQA-Vision, a new vision benchmark from Spanish medical and nursing residency exams to reduce contamination risk.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive benchmarking showing competitive performance versus state-of-the-art models and improved balance between domain-specific and general abilities, using a novel low-contamination evaluation set.
watch_item: The models remain vulnerable to adversarial and misleading inputs, which is a key concern for safety-critical healthcare use.
paper_title: Aloe-Vision: Robust Vision-Language Models for Healthcare
